summary: Cross-functional check-in to align on stability playbook, run-rate spend forecasts, and pilot measurement plan. Customer is concerned about intermittent latency spikes on longer contexts and wants to understand dedicated vs hosted economics. Agreed to run a short benchmark and deliver a 3-scenario cost model.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-05-20
- Start time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Samir Khan (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (CSM); Maya Ortiz (Keystone Head of ML), Rahul Desai (Platform Eng), Olivia Chen (Finance), Tom Baker (SRE)

Topics: stability incidents, cost forecast, pilot scope, security requirements, next steps

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We'll run about 45-55 minutes, want to cover the playbook we put together, run-rate spend models, and field any questions on private vs dedicated deployments.
[00:12] Maya: Yeah thanks Jordan, quick note—sorry if I speak over people, we've had a couple incident windows last month and want to make sure the pilot measures those things.
[00:20] Samir: Got it, can you say briefly what the incidents looked like? Were they per-model cold starts, or something else?
[00:29] Tom: Mostly spikes at 95th and then a couple tail latencies on sequences > 2k tokens. We saw KV cache not helping for some of the chat threads because users send long context with duplicated prefixes.
[00:44] Rahul: Also there was a network flapping event in our VPC that coincided, so it's a little noisy to attribute.
[00:53] Jordan: Makes sense. From our side, the playbook we propose has three lanes—hosted baseline with aggressive batching and prefix caching, a dedicated pool with pinned GPU capacity, and private/VPC deployment for stricter isolation. We'll map each to SLOs and cost.
[01:12] Olivia: Cost is top of mind. Finance wants a realistic run-rate: what the delta looks like between hosted and dedicated when we hit 1M tokens/day.
[01:22] Jordan: Sure—Samir do you want to walk through the initial cost model?
[01:26] Samir: Yep. So quick caveat—these numbers are estimates. Baseline hosted with caching reduces per-token compute by roughly 25-35% for our typical prompt mix. Dedicated with reserved GPUs drops the effective cost another 15-20% but you pay a monthly commit. If you need consistent 99th percentile latency and isolation, dedicated makes sense.
[01:45] Maya: When you say caching, are you talking prefix/kv cache on the runtime or application-level caching?
[01:51] Samir: Runtime-level prefix & KV cache—automatic; also suggestions for application-side dedupe. For long threads we recommended an LRU window with serialized checkpoints to avoid reattaching large prefixes repeatedly.
[02:03] Rahul: Would that change the model quality at all? We're sensitive to hallucination rates as well.
[02:09] Samir: Shouldn't materially affect output—it's mostly cache hits to avoid recomputation. Quantization and batch sizes can slightly change token probabilities but we've seen negligible quality regression with the quant profiles we propose.
[02:23] Tom: On network—if we do a private deploy in our VPC, what's the expected ops overhead? We can't have much maintenance burden.
[02:31] Jordan: Private deployment comes with a customer-managed control plane. We ship an ops bundle and offer a support tier with managed patching. For air-gapped/on-prem we do a handoff doc. Evelyn maybe mention the SLO between tiers?
[02:45] Evelyn: Sure—hosted SLA is typically 99.5% with latency targets per model tier; Dedicated can be 99.9% with reserved throughput. Private can be negotiated depending on infra and patch cadence.
[02:58] Olivia: Are you SOC2 and ISO-aligned? We need those artifacts for procurement.
[03:03] Jordan: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001—I'll share the current attestation and our encryption/KMS whitepaper.
[03:12] Maya: Great. Can you also include audit log samples? We need to map to our compliance controls.
[03:18] Jordan: Yep, action item noted.
[03:22] Samir: Back to performance—let me sketch the benchmark plan: 1) a 48-hour hosted run with 3 synthetic workloads (burst, steady, long-context chat); 2) a dedicated pilot for 7 days with a small commit; 3) capture token-level latency, per-route cost, and tail latencies. We can run with up to 500 concurrent virtual users to stress queuing.
[03:46] Rahul: For the dedicated pilot, can we tune autoscale policies? Some of our traffic is diurnal so we don't want overcommit.
[03:53] Samir: Yes, we can set min/max pools and burst capacities. We'll also provide recommendations on pre-warming KV caches during expected spikes.
[04:03] Tom: Any concerns about data residency? We need logs to remain within us-east-1 for regulatory reasons.
[04:09] Jordan: For hosted we have region controls; the pilot can be pinned to us-east-1. Private deployment of course keeps everything in your VPC.
[04:18] Olivia: On the cost model, please include a sensitivity analysis—what happens if usage doubles vs if caching is 50% effective.
[04:26] Samir: Will do. The three scenarios we'll send: baseline conservative, optimized (with caching + batching), and dedicated committed. We'll show per-token and monthly run-rate.
[04:36] [05:00] Maya: Quick question—we've looked at Replicate and SageMaker. How do you compare on observability and per-route cost transparency?
[05:10] Jordan: Our console exposes token-level cost, per-model breakdowns, route tags, and tracing hooks. You can tie route-level alerts to evals so you get quality drift signals.
[05:21] Samir: Also, our rollout controls include canaries and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency SLOs are missed.
[05:29] Rahul: That fallback—does it degrade model capability or just route to a different quantized variant?
[05:35] Samir: It can be policy-driven: route to a slightly lower-cost quantized variant or fall back to a region with capacity. We can also configure graceful degradation where non-critical routes are downgraded first.
[05:48] Tom: For the benchmark, what telemetry will you need from our side?
[05:53] Samir: We'll need example request shapes, typical sequence length distribution, a distribution of function calls vs plain text, and any auth proxy details. Also, an IAM role or service account for telemetry exports.
[06:07] Maya: We'll prepare that.
[06:10] Olivia: On governance, if we move to dedicated, what's the billing cadence? Is it monthly or annual?
[06:16] Jordan: Both options—monthly reserved capacity or annual with a discount. We'll show the break-even for different commit sizes in the cost model.
[06:25] Maya: Any risks you foresee with our current prompt architecture? We do a lot of few-shot examples inline which pushes token counts up.
[06:34] Samir: Inline few-shot examples blow up tokens. We recommend client-side dynamic examples—pull examples from a short vector store instead of embedding them in the prompt every time. That will dramatically lower per-request tokens.
[06:46] Rahul: Interesting. We have a vector DB but it's on a separate infra—can Redwood's reranker/embedding pipeline connect to our VPC?
[06:54] Jordan: Yes—private connector options and secure peering. We'll document required network rules.
[07:01] Evelyn: I'll add connectors doc to the follow-up bundle.
[07:06] Olivia: From Finance perspective, we need to see the pilot burn scoped to a single product line, with a go/no-go after 30 days.
[07:14] Jordan: That aligns—our pilot proposal can be limited to a single route and tracked. We'll include acceptance criteria: 99th percentile latency < X ms, cost per active user below Y, and no P1 incidents attributed to Redwood.
[07:29] Maya: Can you set the x and y thresholds? We need numbers to put in our scoring rubric.
[07:34] Samir: We'll propose thresholds based on your current 95th/99th baseline; if you share historical percentiles we'll tune them.
[07:41] Tom: One more—how do you handle model rollbacks if a new model increases hallucination?
[07:46] Samir: We have evaluation hooks that compare to baseline prompt sets; automatic rollback can be triggered if quality metrics cross a threshold. It's tied to the rollout policy.
[07:57] Rahul: Do we get logs that map token positions back to customer IDs for debugging? We have PII concerns.
[08:04] Jordan: We mask PII by default and can provide sanitized traces. For debugging, you can opt into reversible logs under strict controls and KMS key access.
[08:15] Olivia: That KMS detail is critical for procurement.
[08:19] Jordan: We'll include KMS key handling and example IAM policies.
[08:24] [08:30] Maya: Okay, sounds good. What's the timeline for the benchmark and cost model?
[08:33] Jordan: We'll send the 3-scenario cost model within 48 hours. Bench plan: start the hosted 48-hour run within a week after we get the sample request shapes and the telemetry role. Dedicated pilot can follow in 2-3 weeks depending on approvals.
[08:48] Olivia: Finance will review the model once it's in.
[08:51] Jordan: Great. Any other concerns?
[08:55] Tom: One small ask—can the playbook include a runbook snippet for dealing with cache invalidation? We had an outage because of stale embeddings.
[09:03] Samir: Absolutely, we'll include cache invalidation patterns and a small runbook for embedding refresh windows.
[09:10] Maya: Also include notes on prompt engineering to reduce token use.
[09:13] Jordan: Will do.
[09:16] Evelyn: I'll summarize next steps in an email and attach the attestation docs.
[09:20] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Quick recap: Jordan to send cost model + compliance docs in 48 hours; Samir to outline benchmark config and batching/caching proposals; Maya/Rahul to provide request shapes and telemetry access; Olivia to confirm budget guardrails. We'll reconvene after the hosted 48-hour run results.
[09:40] Maya: Thanks all.
[09:42] Olivia: Thanks.
[09:43] Jordan: End meeting.

End of transcript.
